# Shared density-event evaluation

This increment joins the qualified recovery and supplied-profile calculus from merged PRs #430/#442 inside the existing C++ field evaluation service. A private qualification factory exercises actual `rho_nm`, selected-reference `eta_true` and `ape` without changing the public variable catalog. APV, public output promotion, writer/restart/append qualification and complete integration performance remain later increments. MATLAB production and saved-file schemas are unchanged.

The event owns current density and its geometry. A typed helper borrows those stable inputs and prepares only requested derived state. Actual-profile recovery and selected-profile inversion are separate dependencies: `rho_nm` remains actual under the explicit initial reference; initial-only displacement/APE bypass recovery. Sequential consumers share completed stages, while each later event/direct invocation receives fresh state. No helper survives solely to serve writer retries, whose existing prepared payloads remain authoritative. Geometry ownership permits individual field plans to be destroyed between coincident consumers.

The existing diagnostic plan stages dependencies and validates all output buffers before numerical work. Failure publishes no active output values. Partial internal stages can remain useful within the same immutable event, with all storage released at event completion. Empty/inactive requests allocate no density-sized storage. Density-only scopes do not populate the unrelated four-volume primitive cache. Explicit capacity metrics include helper vectors, event-owned source/geometry and nested profile/recovery workspace; these are owned vector capacities, not process RSS. Existing numerical operations are unchanged by optional partial-failure workspace reporting.

## Verification ledger

- Release: helper analytic/demand/failure/allocation tests, field-service lifetime/transaction/reference tests and both existing no-motion primitive tests pass (4/4). The field-service controls cover constant Hydrostatic/nonhydrostatic configurations with both antialias settings, unchanged-pointer state mutation, coincident reuse, inactive outputs and late inversion failure.
- ASan/UBSan: the same four focused targets pass (4/4). The two existing field-service/observer tests also pass in both Release and sanitized builds (2/2 each).
- MATLAB: 32 nontrivial comparisons and four independent stable-rest controls pass across four wave-bearing configurations, both antialias modes, actual/initial references and reference/native providers. A distinct sanitized reference build passes 16 nontrivial comparisons and two rest controls. Plan destruction between consumers, exact replay, state immutability and public rejection also pass. Maximum Release/native errors are 6.91216e-11 kg/m^3 in density, 2.44390e-8 m in displacement, and 9.68621e-14 m^2/s^2 in APE; density closure is exact. Each event performs one recovery, profile construction, inverse and APE pass; owned capacity returns to zero. An initial report-accumulator fixture failure was corrected without changing numerical code or tolerances; only the affected method was rerun, and the initial evidence is retained. The changed MATLAB test has zero Code Analyzer findings.
- CI routing/artifact policy passes all 42 tests. One documentation build and comparison pass: 2,026 files, 4,145 routes, zero validation failures and zero generated differences after rebuilding. The sole generated change is the changelog mirror in version history. Independent final production review found no material blocker. Public catalog counts and metadata remain unchanged. Source-bound forward-integration receipts were refreshed against committed source `be09fe47`: all six representative MATLAB methods passed for both reference/native providers (12 cases, 432.76 seconds total), both aggregates passed collection, and the strict committed-receipts regression passed. Source/executable hashes were verified after execution; original receipt bytes and reproducible scripts/logs are retained in `.github/ci-evidence/issue-391-density-event/forward-integration-refresh/`. No validation exceptions or scientific source changes were introduced.

Independent #418 work uses a separate worktree and PR. It distinguishes archived source-derived test inventories from current inventory validation, preserving all original scientific artifacts. It is not a prerequisite for this density implementation branch.
